title: Unbinding one of two sinks on the same stream withdraws the shared Listener declaration
body:
Found by the in-house qualification run of 2026-10-19 on the AX7101 (dev e9cbb676, processor 2cbed0a9).

**Behaviour.**
- Two Stream Inputs are bound to the same talker stream. Both declare the one Listener attribute for that StreamID.
- Unbinding ONE of them sends a Leave for that attribute, 0.07-1.3 s after the UNBIND, although the other sink is still bound and settled on it.
- A Milan peer registrar deregisters on that frame (Milan v1.2 4.2.7.2.2). The DUT's next JoinMt re-registers it about 0.8 s later, so the stream is briefly unreserved.

**Required.**
- IEEE 802.1Q-2018 35.1.2.2: Listeners use MAD_Leave.request "to indicate the Streams that are no longer wanted". The stream is still wanted by the other sink.
- 10.2: one participant per application per end station.
- 10.7.7: one Applicant per attribute value.

**Source.** `hdl/srp/KL_srp_listener_fsm.sv`:
- `:350-360`: the applicant plane is per sink, so two sinks on one StreamID are two applicants for one attribute value;
- `:509-513`: a sink's teardown applies Lv! with no check that another sink declares the same StreamID.

**Done when:**
- a teardown withdraws the Listener attribute only when no other settled sink declares the same StreamID, using a reference count, or one applicant per StreamID;
- suite cases for two sinks on one stream (unbind one, then the other), each with a planted mutant;
- the processor's suites and the parent's consumer gates pass.
